newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong future leader Tung goes house-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong future leader Tung goes house-hunting.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa might take over the home of Britain's colonial military chief after shunning the mansion that has been the traditional home to British governors, a newspaper said on Wednesday.

A spokesman at Tung's office confirmed the Apple Daily report that the billionaire former shipping tycoon was looking for a residence and office but said no decision had been made, barely three months before a century and a half of British rule ends.

Tung snubbed the departing British last year by signalling he would not move into the neo-classic governor's mansion after current occupant Chris Patten departs, saying the building had bad "feng shui", or was out of harmony with its surroundings.

A report in the Apple Daily newspaper said Tung is pondering a takeover of the home of Major General Bryan Dutton, commander of British armed forces in Hong Kong, in the upscale residential area of Victoria Peak.
Dutton will also be moving out as British forces withdraw on June 30 and the territory is returned to China.
But a spokesman for Tung's office said it was not yet known whether the incoming commanders of China's People's Liberation Army garrison would want to use Dutton's residence.
He said the property selected must be government-owned because of the territory's high property prices.
All the best government-owned residential properties were already occupied by senior officials, he said.
